headline: TTWO rockets +8.4% on GTA 6 presale hype while the ASX surges 1.1% and Australian politics heats up with AI regulation and Treasurer leaks.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: GTA 6 is launching next week and presales are, in the CEO's words, 'far in excess' of expectations. CEO Strauss Zelnick also confirmed the game won't be delayed again. The market got very excited — this was the single biggest mover in your portfolio last night.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: AI stocks bounced back today on the ASX, lifting this ETF +2.2%. Broad enthusiasm around AI continues, helped by news of Anthropic's new Claude Fable 5.2 models topping benchmarks. Still down -17.5% overall from your cost base though.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: A strong ASX session today (up 1.1%) lifted VDHG nicely. This broad diversified ETF tracks global markets, so the positive sentiment across both Aussie and international shares pulled it up 2% today.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: VTS tracks the entire US share market in AUD, and today's local session priced in last night's US moves plus AUD/USD stability. Up +1.6% today, sitting just above your cost base now.

movers.name: DHHF (BetaShares Diversified All Growth ETF)
movers.note: Rode the broader ASX rally today, up +1.5%. A diversified global growth ETF — it goes where the market goes, and today the market went up.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: A small +0.7% bump today, but Pilbara remains deeply underwater — down -56.8% from your cost base. Scotiabank this week cut its price target on Albemarle (a bellwether lithium stock) citing a weaker lithium outlook, which is not great news for PLS.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: Barely moved today (+0.2%). Emerging markets have been sluggish — geopolitical uncertainty around the US-Iran situation and a generally cautious global mood are keeping this one flat.

movers.name: Alphabet (Google)
movers.note: Edged up +0.25% last night. Google Cloud posted 103% revenue growth in recent results, well ahead of AWS, which is a big deal. However, JPMorgan removed Alphabet from its Analyst Focus List last night, which may have kept a lid on the gains.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Slipped -0.45% last night — a small dip with no major catalyst. Azure cloud continues to compete hard with Google Cloud, but investors may have rotated slightly after the cloud comparison report showed Google leading on growth rate. Nothing structurally wrong here.

watch_today.title: TTWO: GTA 6 launches next week — hold and enjoy the ride
watch_today.detail: Take-Two surged +8.35% last night after the CEO confirmed GTA 6 presales are 'far in excess' of expectations and the game is definitely not being delayed again. It launches next week. This is the thesis playing out in real time. You're now +4.1% overall on this position. For a long-term holder, sit tight — the real revenue story unfolds post-launch.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX: Lithium outlook stays gloomy — hold, don't add yet
watch_today.detail: Pilbara is down -56.8% from your cost base and Scotiabank just cut its price target on major lithium peer Albemarle this week, citing a weaker lithium price outlook. PLS ticked up +0.69% today but the fundamental headwinds haven't cleared. The long-term EV battery demand story is intact, but there's no rush to add more here — wait for clearer signs of a lithium price floor.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX: AI sector bouncing — hold, thesis intact
watch_today.detail: Up +2.23% today as AI stocks broadly recovered on the ASX. Still down -17.5% from your cost base, but the AI story is very much alive — Anthropic just released Claude Fable 5.2 beating GPT-6 on most benchmarks, and Australia just announced an AI safety regulator, signalling the sector is maturing. Long-term, this ETF is in the right space. Hold.

watch_today.title: RBA watching AI data centre boom — rates may stay higher longer
watch_today.detail: The Reserve Bank warned this week that Australia's AI data centre construction boom is adding inflationary pressure, which could keep interest rates higher for longer. This matters for growth stocks and ETFs — higher rates for longer generally create headwinds. Keep an eye on the RBA's next meeting for any updated guidance.

watch_today.title: US midterms: Democrats take Congress — market uncertainty ahead
watch_today.detail: Democrats won control of Congress in last night's US midterm elections, setting up two years of divided government with Trump still in the White House. Markets last night dipped slightly (S&P -0.55%, NASDAQ -0.61%) as investors weigh what gridlock means for policy. Stephen Miller is now White House Chief of Staff, signalling Trump will push further right. Watch for tariff talk — that's the main risk to your globally-exposed ETFs.

watch_today.title: Storm warning for the Gold Coast tomorrow
watch_today.detail: Weather data shows a hail storm forecast tomorrow with 99% rain chance and 13.8mm expected. Worth knowing if you're heading out on the Coast.

world.summary: The big global stories today: the US-Iran war appears to be winding down after Trump's comments, Democrats flipped Congress in the midterms setting up gridlock, Stephen Miller takes over as White House Chief of Staff, and COP31 climate talks focus on electricity as the key to breaking the deadlock.

stories.title: Trump says US-Iran war is 'effectively over' militarily after Qatar talks
stories.why_it_matters: After meeting Qatar's Prime Minister, Trump said the US-Iran war is 'effectively over' from a military standpoint and that further US attacks on Iran are 'highly unlikely'. This is significant because it signals a potential de-escalation of a conflict that has rattled oil markets and global security for months. European diplomats are reportedly upbeat following the update on peace talks. If this holds, it could ease oil price volatility — crude already slipped -1.73% last night to US$85.35.

stories.title: Democrats win US midterm elections — divided government until 2029
stories.why_it_matters: Democrats took back control of Congress in the US midterm elections, flipping both the House and Senate. This creates a divided government — Trump is still president but now faces a Democratic-controlled legislature that can block his agenda. Democrats say they'll prioritise healthcare and tariff reform, and have explicitly ruled out pursuing Trump's impeachment. For investors, divided government typically means less dramatic policy swings, which markets often like — but tariff battles remain a real risk.

stories.title: Hardline Trump aide Stephen Miller appointed White House Chief of Staff
stories.why_it_matters: Trump has appointed Stephen Miller — one of his most hardline advisers, known for his hardline immigration and nationalist policy positions — as White House Chief of Staff. Miller is widely seen as a loyalist who will push Trump further to the right. This follows the midterm results and signals that despite losing Congress, Trump plans to use executive power aggressively. Miller's appointment could mean a more combative White House approach to trade and immigration policy.

stories.title: Trump claims elections were 'rigged', questions midterm results
stories.why_it_matters: Despite early results showing Democratic gains, Trump has returned to claiming the elections are 'rigged', a repeat of his 2020 and 2024 playbook. He's described the US as having taken a 'giant step back'. Political analysts warn this could inflame his base and create instability heading into the new Congress. Markets tend to dislike political uncertainty — this is worth watching.

stories.title: COP31 climate talks: electricity seen as the key to breaking the deadlock
stories.why_it_matters: COP31 climate negotiations are underway, and diplomats are increasingly betting that a global push to triple electricity capacity — particularly renewables — is the most politically achievable path to breaking the climate policy deadlock. Australia is hosting COP31 this year, so this is particularly relevant. A global electricity buildout has long-term implications for energy stocks, materials (lithium, copper) and infrastructure investment.

markets.summary: The ASX had a strong day, closing up +1.1% to 9,129. Last night on Wall Street, the S&P 500 slipped -0.55% and the NASDAQ fell -0.61% — likely a reaction to the US midterm results and ongoing uncertainty. Gold fell -1.3% and oil dropped -1.7%, while the Aussie dollar was essentially flat at US$0.6867.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Strong local session today — broad-based gains across the board.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Slipped last night, likely as markets digested the US midterm results and what divided government means for policy.

indicators.name: NASDAQ
indicators.note: Tech stocks gave back a little ground last night. Modest dip, nothing alarming.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Oil fell after Trump said the US-Iran war is 'effectively over' — less conflict risk means less fear of supply disruption.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Gold pulled back as some of the geopolitical risk premium came off with the Iran war commentary.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: Essentially unchanged. The Aussie dollar is holding steady.

politics.summary: A big day in Australian politics: the Albanese government announced new mandatory AI regulations and a dedicated AI safety regulator after OpenAI hacked Medicare data, while internal Labor tensions over Treasurer Jim Chalmers continue to bubble up publicly. The RBA also warned the AI data centre construction boom could keep interest rates higher for longer.

stories.title: Australia to create AI safety regulator with mandatory reporting rules after OpenAI hacked Medicare
stories.why_it_matters: The Albanese government announced it will create a new AI Safety Regulator and introduce mandatory rules requiring AI companies to report security incidents — triggered by a breach in which OpenAI accessed Medicare data. Companies that fail to comply could face criminal penalties under proposed law changes. This is a significant step toward regulating AI in Australia and means companies operating AI systems here will face new legal obligations. It directly affects tech giants like Google and Microsoft which your portfolio holds.

stories.title: Jim Chalmers under fire as Labor colleagues leak against Treasurer
stories.why_it_matters: Internal Labor tensions are boiling over, with colleagues reportedly leaking against Treasurer Jim Chalmers to the media. Environment Minister Tanya Plibersek publicly urged Labor colleagues to stop undermining Chalmers. Reports suggest Treasury has been 'silenced' on some key economic policy debates. This internal dysfunction is a distraction at a time when business groups are urging the government to 'act now, act big' on economic policy.

stories.title: RBA warns AI data centre boom could keep interest rates higher for longer
stories.why_it_matters: The Reserve Bank has flagged that the surge in AI data centre construction across Australia is driving energy demand and creating inflationary pressure, which could mean interest rates stay higher for longer. This is a double-edged sword: it's good for the energy sector but bad news for anyone with a mortgage or a growth-oriented portfolio. The RBA is effectively saying that the AI boom itself is adding to the cost-of-living crunch.

stories.title: Teals rush donations ahead of controversial new political funding rules
stories.why_it_matters: Independent 'teal' MPs are rushing to bank donations ahead of new political funding laws set to take effect. The new rules are expected to restrict or cap the ability of wealthy donors to fund independent campaigns. The teals — who hold the balance of power in several key electorates — are treating this as urgent, suggesting they expect the rules to significantly cut their funding advantage. This could reshape the political landscape at the next federal election.

ai.summary: A busy day in AI: Australia just created a new AI safety regulator triggered by an OpenAI Medicare breach, Anthropic released powerful new Claude models beating GPT-6 on most benchmarks, and the big cloud providers are in a fierce race with Google Cloud now leading on growth.

stories.title: Australia mandates AI breach reporting, creates safety regulator after OpenAI hacked Medicare
stories.why_it_matters: The Albanese government announced Australia will create a dedicated AI Safety Regulator and require AI companies to mandatorily report any security incidents — a direct response to OpenAI accessing Medicare data in a breach. The government is also considering criminal law changes to hold 'frontier' AI companies (the most advanced AI developers) legally accountable. This is one of the most significant AI governance moves in Australia's history, putting Australia alongside the EU and UK in building formal AI oversight.

stories.title: Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 — beats GPT-6 and Gemini 4 on most benchmarks
stories.why_it_matters: Anthropic just dropped two new AI models — Claude Fable 5.2 (designed for storytelling and creative tasks) and Mythos 5.2 (aimed at complex reasoning and coding). Both outperformed OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra and Google's Gemini 4 Carbon on most standard benchmarks. This matters because it shows the AI race is tightening fast — Anthropic (backed by Google and Amazon) is now a genuine frontrunner, which puts pressure on both GOOG and MSFT to keep pace.

stories.title: Google Cloud leads with 103% revenue growth in cloud comparison vs AWS and Azure
stories.why_it_matters: A major cloud comparison report shows Google Cloud growing at 103% year-on-year — the fastest of the three big cloud providers. Amazon's AWS still leads in total scale, and Microsoft Azure is competitive, but Google is closing the gap at an extraordinary pace. For your GOOG holding, this is the key growth engine to watch: cloud is where the big money is in tech right now, and Google is winning on growth rate.

stories.title: Orange telecom launches apps combining Claude, Gemini, Mistral and GPT in one place
stories.why_it_matters: French telco Orange launched 'Orange IAs' — a suite of consumer apps that lets users access Claude (Anthropic), Gemini (Google), Mistral, and ChatGPT (OpenAI) all in one place. Think of it as a TV remote control for AI — switching between models depending on what you need. This kind of multi-model consumer product signals AI is moving from novelty to everyday utility, and that distribution (getting AI into apps people already use) is becoming as important as the models themselves.

sport.summary: The NRL Grand Final saw the Roosters pip the Knights 19-18 in a thriller at Accor Stadium. Off the field, Roosters prop Junior Papalii's rep teammate Stefano Utoikamanu was banned for two matches for a money gesture to referees, and the Rugby League World Cup announced a travelling Magic Round format for 2030. In tennis, Jannik Sinner is targeting the Australian Open as his comeback from injury.

stories.title: NRL Grand Final: Roosters beat Knights 19-18 in a one-point thriller
stories.why_it_matters: The Sydney Roosters won the 2026 NRL premiership by the narrowest possible margin, defeating the Newcastle Knights 19-18 at Accor Stadium. One point separated the two sides at the final whistle — it doesn't get more dramatic than that. The Roosters claimed their latest title in what will go down as one of the great Grand Finals.

stories.title: Leniu handed two-match ban after money gesture to referees
stories.why_it_matters: NRL player Leniu has been given a two-match ban after making a money gesture at referees during a match — a gesture interpreted as implying the refs had been paid off. The NRL came down hard on the act as part of its ongoing push to protect officials. The ban takes effect immediately.

stories.title: Rugby League World Cup 2030 adopts travelling Magic Round format
stories.why_it_matters: The Rugby League World Cup 2030 has confirmed it will use a 'travelling Magic Round' format — where multiple games are played at the same venue over a weekend, rotating between host cities. This is the first time the World Cup has adopted the format made popular by the NRL's domestic Magic Round event. It's designed to create festival-style atmospheres and boost attendance and TV ratings.

stories.title: Jannik Sinner targets Australian Open comeback from injury
stories.why_it_matters: Former world No.1 Jannik Sinner has set his sights on returning to competitive tennis at the Australian Open in January. Sinner has been sidelined with injury and says he won't rush his recovery, but is positive about being ready for Melbourne. He's also hinted he wants to continue playing well into his 30s. His return would be a massive boost for the Australian Open, where he's been a crowd favourite.

stories.title: Broncos star learns fate after NRL hands down drink driving ban
stories.why_it_matters: A Brisbane Broncos player has received a ban from the NRL following a drink driving charge. The article confirms the penalty has been handed down. The NRL has been increasingly firm on off-field conduct issues this season, and this case is part of that broader pattern. The specific length of the ban and the player's name were not included in the available article text.
